critique.paragraph: The map's spatial grammar—discrete purple wireframe grid suspended in black void—sets up the continuous-discrete tension, but the plate fails because its teaching artifacts are missing or non-functional. The blurb promises floating hands in a mirror with nail customization, yet the screenshots show only placeholder cubes and error messages about a missing color_picker. Without the body fragments (VR hands), the mirror reflection, or the personalization mechanic, the plate reads as an empty test scene rather than a diagram of embodiment's algorithmic mismatch. The void and grid are cousins to Marey's chronophotographic frames, but without the body plotted across them, there's no argument.
strengths: Void + grid contrast effectively stages discrete geometry against continuous darkness
Minimalist spatial grammar could support Vitruvian/Marey-style body-as-diagram composition
10×10 dimensions keep focus tight on central teaching moment
weaknesses: Missing color_picker artifact (unknown_lookup_name) breaks the customization teaching mechanic entirely
No visible VR hand models in any angle—the core 'body as fragments' claim is absent
Mirror artifact present but not visibly reflecting hands or demonstrating the quantized self-image
Reads as Edge A (grid foundations) or as no edge at all—empty staging with no body-algorithm tension
Placeholder cubes (pink/red) occlude what should be the teaching focal point
next_gen_hints: Fix color_picker artifact reference—ensure it spawns and is reachable from spawn point
Add VR hand models at spawn or as ghost poses frozen in mid-gesture—make the 'fragments in void' literal
Position mirror at eye level, 2-3 cells from spawn, facing player—reflection should be unavoidable first sight
Mirror surface should show hands clearly, possibly with grid overlay or wireframe skin to emphasize quantization
Replace placeholder cubes with the actual teaching artifacts or remove them entirely
Consider dual mirrors: one showing continuous hand tracking, one showing grid-snapped positions—the mismatch IS the plate
